finding: rocq dep and Rocq compilation may read comments differently, which can omit or add a dependency edge.
classification: Dependency-consistency mechanism test, not an old successful false-proof bypass.
old_baseline_claim: The reported stale dependency causes an inconsistent-assumptions failure. No successful false proof on 0ec5fcd is claimed by this coverage record.
mechanisms: Rocq records dependency digests in .vo files and refuses a dependent module when the loaded dependency differs.
The release requires a fresh full rebuild, independently of this isolated test.

dedicated_test.toolchain: rocq and rocqchk 9.1.1, checked by the script
dedicated_test.fixtures: Fresh A.v, B.v requiring A, and a loading probe under build/dependency-tests/run-*; definitions and reflexivity only.
checks: Compile A and B, then load B and check it with rocqchk successfully.
Change A.value from 0 to 1 and compile only A; verify A.vo changed and B.vo did not.
Loading stale B and checking stale B must each fail with the specific inconsistent-assumptions diagnostic.
Rebuild B, verify B.vo changes, then repeat loading and kernel checking successfully.
dedicated_test.evidence: Each run writes result.json, exact commands, object hashes and separate stdout/stderr logs beneath its fresh scratch directory.
dedicated_test.measured_result: All 10 checked steps passed locally on Rocq 9.1.1.

limits: This test exercises the safety mechanism after a missed rebuild; it does not reproduce the distinct rocq dep comment-parser discrepancy.
It does not replace the clean project rebuild, source scans, snapshot checks or report checks.
No project module, Elpi program, unsafe Rocq feature or full project build is executed by this test.
